units.label: Verse 1
units.deva:
नाहं देहो नेन्द्रियाण्यन्तरङ्गो नाहंकारः प्राणवर्गो न बुद्धिः ।
दारापत्यक्षेत्रवित्तादिदूरः साक्षी नित्यः प्रत्यगात्मा शिवोऽहम् ॥
units.translation: I am not the body, the sense faculties, the inner mind, the ego, the vital breaths, or the intellect. I am far removed from spouse, children, land, wealth, and the rest. I am the eternal witness, the inward Self—Śiva.
units.iast:
nāhaṃ deho nendriyāṇyantaraṅgo nāhaṃkāraḥ prāṇavargo na buddhiḥ |
dārāpatyakṣetravittādidūraḥ sākṣī nityaḥ pratyagātmā śivo’ham ||

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
रज्ज्वज्ञानाद्भाति रज्जौ यथाहिः स्वात्माज्ञानादात्मनो जीवभावः ।
आप्तोक्त्याहिभ्रान्तिनाशे स रज्जुर्जीवो नाहं देशिकोक्त्या शिवोऽहम् ॥
units.translation: Just as a snake appears on a rope through ignorance of the rope, so the Self seems to be an individual soul through ignorance of one’s own Self. When a trustworthy statement dispels the snake-delusion, that [appearance] is a rope. By the teacher’s statement, I am not the individual soul; I am Śiva.

gloss.en: from ignorance of one’s own Self

units.iast:
rajjvajñānādbhāti rajjau yathāhiḥ svātmājñānādātmano jīvabhāvaḥ |
āptoktyāhibhrāntināśe sa rajjurjīvo nāhaṃ deśikoktyā śivo’ham ||

units.label: Verse 3
units.deva:
आभातीदं विश्वमात्मन्यसत्यं सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपे विमोहात् ।
निद्रामोहात्स्वप्नवत्तन्न सत्यं शुद्धः पूर्णो नित्य एकः शिवोऽहम् ॥
units.translation: Through delusion, this unreal universe appears in the Self, whose nature is reality, knowledge, and bliss. Like a dream from the delusion of sleep, it is not real. I am pure, complete, eternal, one—Śiva.

gloss.en: in whose nature are reality • knowledge • bliss

units.iast:
ābhātīdaṃ viśvamātmanyasatyaṃ satyajñānānandarūpe vimohāt |
nidrāmohātsvapnavattanna satyaṃ śuddhaḥ pūrṇo nitya ekaḥ śivo’ham ||

units.label: Verse 4
units.deva:
नाहं जातो न प्रवृद्धो न नष्टो देहस्योक्ताः प्राकृताः सर्वधर्माः ।
कर्तृत्वादिश्चिन्मयस्यास्ति नाहंकारस्यैव ह्यात्मनो मे शिवोऽहम् ॥
units.translation: I am not born, do not grow, and am not destroyed; all these natural properties are said to belong to the body. Doership and the rest—do they belong to the conscious Self? No: they belong to the ego alone. As for my Self, I am Śiva.
units.iast:
nāhaṃ jāto na pravṛddho na naṣṭo dehasyoktāḥ prākṛtāḥ sarvadharmāḥ |
kartṛtvādiścinmayasyāsti nāhaṃkārasyaiva hyātmano me śivo’ham ||

units.label: Verse 5
units.deva:
मत्तो नान्यत्किंचिदत्रास्ति विश्वं सत्यं बाह्यं वस्तु मायोपकॢप्तम् ।
आदर्शान्तर्भासमानस्य तुल्यं मय्यद्वैते भाति तस्माच्छिवोऽहम् ॥
units.translation: There is nothing at all here apart from me. The universe, taken as a real external object, is fashioned by māyā. It appears in me, the non-dual Self, like what shines within a mirror; therefore I am Śiva.
units.iast:
matto nānyatkiṃcidatrāsti viśvaṃ satyaṃ bāhyaṃ vastu māyopakḷptam |
ādarśāntarbhāsamānasya tulyaṃ mayyadvaite bhāti tasmācchivo’ham ||

units.label: Closing colophon
units.deva: इति श्रीमत्परमहंसपरिव्राजकाचार्यस्य श्रीगोविन्दभगवत्पूज्यपादशिष्यस्य श्रीमच्छङ्करभगवतः कृतौ अद्वैतपञ्चरत्नं संपूर्णम् ॥
units.translation: Thus is complete the Advaitapañcaratnam, composed by the revered Śaṅkara Bhagavat, supreme renunciant and teacher among wandering ascetics, disciple of the worship-worthy feet of Govinda Bhagavat.

gloss.en: of the teacher among wandering ascetics
whose feet are worthy of worship

units.iast: iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau advaitapañcaratnaṃ saṃpūrṇam ||
